subject: Infinitely weighted logistic regression / point process models in JAGS?

messages.author: 9ef60fd1c92630ce
messages.subject: Infinitely weighted logistic regression / point process models in JAGS?
parts:
Greetings All,
I was wondering if anyone has experience writing up point process models (or infinitely weighted logistic regression) using JAGS as in "Point process models for presence only analysis" <https://besjournals.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1111/2041-210X.12352> ? Is it possible to include weights in JAGS specification to run the weighted regression?
Cheers,

messages.author: 00ebeb6e0521112d
messages.subject: AW: Infinitely weighted logistic regression / point process models in JAGS?
parts:
Hi Erica,

 

In our upcoming AHM2 book, we have a Bayesian implementation of a point pattern model as a Bernoulli GLM with offset equal to the log of the pixel area, when you discretize space into very small units such that each contains ideally at most 1 point (see Baddeley et al. 2010, Electronic Journal of Statistics). This works pretty well, presumably unless you have much more than 10,000 pixels.

 

Best regards  --- Marc

parts:
Dear Erica,

 

Both in JAGS, yes, I am also rather emotionally attached to it :)

 

Zeroes trick is, as the ones trick, a way to implement any likelihood for which there is no canned function in WinBUGS, OpenBUGS, JAGS (or presumaby any other stats program)

 

Best regards  ---  Marc

Von: Richard Chandler [mailto:richard....@gmail.com]
Gesendet: Donnerstag, 8. August 2019 15:59
An: Erica Stuber
Cc: Kery Marc; hmecology: Hierarchical Modeling in Ecology
Betreff: Re: Infinitely weighted logistic regression / point process models in JAGS?

 

Yes, it works well in JAGS. 

 

On Thu, Aug 8, 2019 at 9:56 AM Erica Stuber <efst...@gmail.com> wrote:

Thanks for your responses Marc and Richard,

Marc: Is your forthcoming AHM2 implementation in JAGS or something else?

Richard: I don't know the zeros trick, but will look around for the code - do you know whether the 'trick' also works in JAGS?

(maybe I'm overly attached to JAGS...)

I sometimes work with high-resolution global extent data, so sample size will likely be an issue at some point for me..

-------------------------
Erica Stuber, PhD

Department of Ecology and Evolutionary Biology

Max Planck - Yale Center for Biodiversity Movement and Global Change

Yale University

165 Prospect St.

New Haven, CT 06520

 

 

 

On Thu, Aug 8, 2019 at 9:48 AM Kery Marc <marc...@vogelwarte.ch> wrote:

Dear Richard,

 

would be interesting to find out what is more efficient in JAGS, or with which one can do bigger sample sizes.

 

Best regards  -- Marc

 

 

Von: Richard Chandler [mailto:richard....@gmail.com]
Gesendet: Donnerstag, 8. August 2019 15:42
An: Kery Marc
Cc: Erica Stuber; hmecology: Hierarchical Modeling in Ecology
Betreff: Re: Infinitely weighted logistic regression / point process models in JAGS?

 

Hi Erica,

 

It's also possible to fit point process models in BUGS using the "zeros trick". There should be code floating around somewhere online, but let me know if you can't find any.

 

Richard

 

 

On Thu, Aug 8, 2019 at 9:05 AM Kery Marc <marc...@vogelwarte.ch> wrote:

Hi Erica,

 

In our upcoming AHM2 book, we have a Bayesian implementation of a point pattern model as a Bernoulli GLM with offset equal to the log of the pixel area, when you discretize space into very small units such that each contains ideally at most 1 point (see Baddeley et al. 2010, Electronic Journal of Statistics). This works pretty well, presumably unless you have much more than 10,000 pixels.

 

Best regards  --- Marc
